request.statement:
Define `simulate_resolution(requests, durations, limit)`.

`requests` contains at most 200,000 tuples `(arrival, family, name, cancel)` in arbitrary order. `arrival` is a nonnegative integer; `family` is an integer; `name` is ASCII with at most 1000 characters; and `cancel` is `None` or an integer at least `arrival`. A request's identity is its zero-based position. `limit` is a positive integer and is the maximum number of simultaneously running jobs.

At each integer time, process all running-job completions by job ID, then start queued work as described below, then process arrivals by request identity, then process cancellations by request identity, and finally start queued work again. A completion therefore wins a simultaneous cancellation.

An empty `name` immediately produces `("error", "EMPTY")`. Otherwise, a family outside `{0, 4, 6}` immediately produces `("error", "INVALID_FAMILY")`.

A literal address bypasses jobs and queues. IPv4 literals have four decimal components in `[0,255]`, without leading zeroes except `0`. IPv6 literals use conventional hexadecimal IPv6 notation, including optional `::` compression and an optional embedded IPv4 literal. An IPv6 literal may have one `%zone` suffix containing 1 through 15 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, or periods; preserve this suffix. Family `0` accepts either version. A mismatching family produces `("error", "ADDRESS_FAMILY")`; otherwise produce `("literal", name)`.

Every other name is treated as DNS. Remove one trailing period, lowercase ASCII letters, and require a resulting length of 1 through 253. Each dot-separated label must contain 1 through 63 letters, digits, or hyphens and may not begin or end with a hyphen. Failure immediately produces `("error", "INVALID_NAME")`.

A valid DNS request has key `(family, normalized_name)`. `durations` maps every requested valid key to a positive integer. If that key has a running job, the caller joins it. Otherwise, if the key already has a queued group, the caller joins that group. Otherwise, if fewer than `limit` jobs are running, create a running job immediately. If the limit is reached, create a queued group. Queued groups have permanent FIFO priority by their creation order.

Whenever queued work is started, repeatedly take the oldest nonempty queued group until the limit is reached or no group remains. Each taken group creates one job at the current time containing all its current callers. Jobs receive consecutive IDs when created, including when created from a queue, and complete after the mapped duration.

On completion, every waiting caller receives `("resolved", job_id, completion_time)`. Cancellation affects only its caller: an unresolved running or queued caller receives `("canceled", cancel_time)` and leaves its job or group. An empty queued group disappears. An empty running job is immediately canceled and removed; capacity released during the cancellation phase is filled only after all cancellations at that time.

Return `(outcomes, jobs)`. `outcomes` is indexed by request identity. `jobs` is in ID order, with records `(job_id, family, normalized_name, start_time, stop_time, status)`, where status is `"completed"` or `"canceled"`. Use only the Python standard library and perform no I/O.
